messages:
maria.chen: Heads up — customer reported p99 latency jump for /v1/generate. Dashboard shows ~2.8s p99, raw histogram from logs shows ~1.1s. Can someone sanity-check?
kevin.tran: saw alert too. Which dashboard panel are you looking at? screenshot?
lisa_analyst: I pulled the dashboard and the panel is using `rollup_quantiles(avg_latency_ms, window=10s)` (dashboard v2). Raw histogram query was `histogram(latency_ms, 50ms)` from ingest.
jordan.patel: if dashboard uses rollup quantiles we may be double-averaging. But that wouldn't increase p99 that much unless samples got truncated.
maria.chen: attaching short extract from customer's trace logs: request id 9f2a.. shows stable 0.9-1.3s. They see 2.5-3s on dashboard.
support-eng: customer also reported a spike during 02:03-02:07 UTC; they sent traces.
kevin.tran: quick hypothesis: our metrics ingestion truncates sub-ms to ms in rollup stage. If we floor to ms, small tails can be pushed into higher buckets for quantile approximations.
infra-ryan: I can check the ingest pipeline. Which producer? metrics-proxy v3.1. We rolled a change last week that altered sample weighting.
lisa_analyst: query I used for raw histo (from logs cluster):
```
SELECT histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
FROM logs_latency
```
This yields ~1.12s at 02:05.
kevin.tran: dashboard panel is using metrics-rollup dataset. Panel config: `source: rollup, method: approx-tdigest, precision: 100, bucket_ms: 1`
jordan.patel: look at `bucket_ms: 1` — that suggests we coarsen to 1ms. But going from micro to ms shouldn't add >1s. Something else: we changed the rollup quantile algorithm to use streaming TDigest with sample weights last deploy. If weights are mis-assigned (e.g., weight=duration instead of 1), p99 will inflate.
infra-ryan: checking deploy logs... deploy of metrics-rollup v1.3.0 at 2026-03-02T01:45:12Z. It included flag `enable_sample_weighting=true`
sre-bot: alert created: p99_latency_high (/v1/generate) @ 2026-03-02T02:06:18Z — alert id A-4391
maria.chen: okay can someone run a backfill query comparing unweighted vs weighted rollup over the spike window?
kevin.tran: running quick check against rollup DB: `SELECT approx_quantile(0.99, values) FILTER(weight IS NULL) AS unweighted, approx_quantile(0.99, values, weight) AS weighted FROM rollup_latency WHERE time BETWEEN '2026-03-02 02:00' AND '2026-03-02 02:08'` — raw shows unweighted 1.15s, weighted 2.9s.
lisa_analyst: that matches customer numbers =
 janky weighting assignment. Looks like some events got weight equal to latency_ms instead of 1.
jordan.patel: that explains it. If sampling weight = latency_ms then long tails are amplified. Likely bug in the aggregator where we accidentally set `sample.weight = sample.value` when `enable_sample_weighting=true` and value unit is ms.
infra-ryan: prepared a patch to fix assignation and a rollback plan. Options: 1) hotfix aggregator to compute weight correctly (fast) 2) revert flag `enable_sample_weighting` (safer) 3) update dashboards to use raw histograms until backfill.
support-eng: customer wants ETA to be fixed; they're sensitive to SLOs.
kevin.tran: mitigation plan: revert flag immediately (1), deploy fix to aggregator for correctness (2) during maintenance window, and add a dashboard annotation + alert mute until we confirm.
maria.chen: runbook for revert: `kubectl set env deploy/metrics-rollup ENABLE_SAMPLE_WEIGHTING=false -n telemetry && kubectl rollout restart deploy/metrics-rollup -n telemetry` — who can run?
infra-ryan: I can run that now, but will coordinate with oncall. Doing a canary first on telemetry-staging then prod.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary release started for metrics-rollup on telemetry-staging @ 2026-03-02T02:18:11Z
kevin.tran: good. Also add an internal note to not trust rollup quantiles for alerts until we confirm. Change alert query to use logs-derived histogram for 24h as fallback:
```
alert_query = "histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(logs_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 2.0"
```
This reduces false positives while we fix ingest.
jordan.patel: we should also add a postmortem tag: root cause = incorrect sample weight assignment in rollup aggregator. Impact = inflated p99 for rollup-backed dashboards and alerts ~ 30 customers.
lisa_analyst: I'll start collecting affected dash panels and notify product owners.
maria.chen: customer update: will tell them we found the cause, reverting rollup weighting now, ETA 30m for canary + 60m to validate, then follow up.
infra-ryan: canary completed on staging, no regressions. Rolling out to prod now.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: rollout to telemetry-prod started @ 2026-03-02T02:33:02Z
infra-ryan: prod rollout done. Reverted `ENABLE_SAMPLE_WEIGHTING` and restarted pods.
kevin.tran: re-querying rollup after revert shows p99 back to ~1.2s. Good.
maria.chen: I'll send the customer the rollback note and temporary dashboard link using logs histograms.
support-eng: customer acknowledged and will monitor. They asked for ETA on a permanent fix/backfill.
jordan.patel: we'll schedule a patch to properly implement weighting semantics and a backfill script to recompute rollups for the affected time range. Add regression test for weighting.
kevin.tran: follow-ups: PR for fix + unit tests (kevin), backfill plan (lisa & infra-ryan), update alerts (maria), postmortem (jordan).
maria.chen: thanks all. closing thread once postmortem PR is in. :thumbsup:
